decisions.reason: A classic lever handle line sits squarely within the firm's core design and fixing know-how, so it can read early market feedback well and refine the line cheaply rather than withdraw it after one year.

This multi-model handle family builds directly on established competencies and certified systems, and architectural hardware is normally sold over long lifecycles, so dropping it within a year is unlikely.
A single handle design close to the core offer is easy to assimilate into the range; its slightly narrower scope makes withdrawal a bit more likely, but one year is too short to judge it.
Like C, this design fits the firm's ergonomic and design expertise and costs little to keep listed, so there is little reason to cut it so soon after launch.
A lever handle family with several models that draws on the firm's existing knowledge base strengthens system breadth and is expected to stay in the range.

The flagship electronic access system with its distinctive light technology matches the strategic move toward digital building organization, and in-house R&D gives the firm the capacity to develop it further.
